speaker: Leonard
text: It's sad how great that sounds. Fine. You can have it back. As long as he promises to make me a hobbit in his next movie.

speaker: Sheldon
text: It's stolen. It should go back to Peter Jackson. He made the movies. It belongs to him. But there are no Jewish hobbits.

speaker: Leonard
text: Clearly you've never been to my house for dinner on Rosh Hashanah.

speaker: Sheldon
text: We are not blackmailing Peter Jackson. You mean my ring?

speaker: Sheldon
text: The ring was unguarded. It was just sitting on the table. Anyone could have taken it. I did. Look, let's be reasonable. We all want to do different things with the ring, but your ideas are stupid, and I want a jet ski.

speaker: Leonard
text: I found it. The ring is mine. I don't understand why in this group I never get my way. You always get your way.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'll stipulate to that if you give me the ring.

speaker: Leonard
text: Yeah, it's delicious. Sarcasm's a little stale, though. Hey, how about this? Until we figure out what to do with the ring, Penny holds on to it.

speaker: Penny
text: Enjoying your food that I actually brought you instead of promising food but bringing you a box of random crap? What ring?

speaker: Leonard
text: This ring. Looking for something? Will you hold on to this for a couple of days? It's a prop from a movie. We're kind of fighting over it.

speaker: Penny
text: Okay, just to be clear, the first piece of jewelry my boyfriend gives me is a prop from a movie and I don't even get to keep it.

speaker: Leonard
text: If you had done that with me three years ago, by now you'd have my great aunt Ida's brooch that she smuggled out of occupied Belgium in a cap.
